p.src: Now, after Ladies Xing and Wang had heard what Madam You had to say, they knew that the matter could hardly be reversed. Lady Wang could only say, “If you wish to devote yourself to virtue, child, it must be a disposition rooted in a former life, and indeed we cannot prevent you. But for a young lady of a family such as ours to become a nun would hardly be seemly. Now that your sister-in-law has consented to let you cultivate the religious life, however, that is well enough. There is just one thing I must say: you need not shave your head. So long as your heart is sincere, what difference can the hair make? Remember that Miaoyu also practiced with her hair unshorn; yet somehow her worldly passions were stirred, and that was what brought her to such a pass. Since you are resolved upon this, we shall regard your present rooms as your religious retreat. We must also summon all your attendants and ask them: whoever wishes to follow you must give up all talk of betrothal or marriage, while those unwilling to follow must make other plans.” Hearing this, Xichun dried her tears and bowed her thanks to Ladies Xing and Wang, Li Wan, Madam You, and the others. Having said this, Lady Wang asked Caiping and the others which of them wished to follow their young mistress into the religious life. Caiping and the others replied, “Whoever the ladies appoint will go.” Lady Wang understood that none of them was willing and was considering whom to choose. Xiren stood behind Baoyu, expecting him to burst into violent tears and watching lest his old illness recur. But to her surprise Baoyu merely sighed, “Truly admirable.” This made Xiren still more heartsick. Though Baochai said nothing, she had tested him whenever occasion arose; seeing that he remained hopelessly obsessed, she could only shed tears in secret. Lady Wang was just about to summon all the maids and question them. Suddenly Zijuan stepped forward, knelt before Lady Wang, and said, “Madam, you were just asking about a maid to accompany Fourth Miss. What would you think of me?” Lady Wang replied, “How could anyone be forced into such a thing? Whoever is willing will naturally speak up.” Zijuan said, “It is naturally the young mistress herself who wishes to enter the religious life; that does not mean the other maids share her intention. I have something to tell you, Madam. I do not mean to set myself apart from the others, but each person has her own heart. I served Miss Lin, and you ladies all know how she treated me. Her kindness was truly weightier than a mountain, and I have no way to repay it. When she died, I longed to follow her in death. But she was not of this household, while I had received the bounty of my masters here, so I could not die with her. Now that Fourth Miss intends to cultivate the religious life, I beg you ladies to assign me to accompany her and serve her for the rest of my life. I do not know whether you will permit it. If you do, it will be my great good fortune.” Before Ladies Xing and Wang could reply, Baoyu, who had heard her words and been reminded of Daiyu, felt a sudden pang in his heart, and tears were already streaming down his face.

p.src: Just as everyone was about to question him, he suddenly roared with laughter, stepped forward, and said, “It is not for me to speak. But since you, Madam, assigned Zijuan to my rooms, I venture to say this. Please grant her request, Madam, and let her fulfill her worthy intention.” Lady Wang said, “When your sisters married, you wept as though your very life were ending. Yet now, when you see your fourth sister about to renounce the world, not only do you make no attempt to dissuade her, but you call it a good thing. What in the world do you mean? I simply cannot understand you anymore.” Baoyu replied, “Fourth Sister’s religious life has already been approved, and she herself is firmly resolved upon it. If she is truly resolved, I have something to tell you, Madam; but if her mind is not fixed, I would not dare talk nonsense.” Xichun said, “Second Brother, what a strange thing to say! If my mind were not made up, could I have prevailed upon the ladies? I say the same as Zijuan: if they permit me, it will be my good fortune; if they do not— there is still death. What is there to fear? If you have something to say, Second Brother, then say it freely.” Baoyu said, “What I am about to say can hardly count as revealing a secret, for this too is something already determined. Let me recite a poem for you!” The others said, “At a time when someone is in such distress, you take it into your head to compose poetry. How exasperating!” Baoyu replied, “I did not compose it. I saw it at a place I visited. Just listen.” They said, “Very well. Recite it, then, but do not improvise some nonsense.” Baoyu made no defense, but began:

p.src: Li Wan and Baochai were astonished to hear this. “This is dreadful—he has become obsessed!” they exclaimed. Lady Wang heard them, nodded with a sigh, and asked Baoyu, “Where exactly did you see it?” Baoyu could not conveniently reveal it and replied, “You need not ask, Mother. I have my own source.” Lady Wang grasped his meaning and, after thinking it over carefully, began to weep still harder. “You said the other day that it was only a joke, so how has this poem suddenly appeared? Very well, now I understand. What do you expect me to do? There is nothing I can do; I shall simply have to let you have your way! But wait until I have closed my eyes forever; then each of you may do as you please, and that will be the end of it!” Baochai tried to comfort her, but her own heart was in even greater agony. Unable to contain herself, she burst into loud sobs. Xiren had already wept herself nearly senseless and was kept on her feet only by Qiuwen’s support. Baoyu neither wept nor offered consolation; he merely remained silent. Having heard this much, Jia Lan and Jia Huan each went away. Li Wan did her utmost to explain: “Brother Bao must have been deeply distressed at seeing Fourth Sister enter the religious life, and so he spoke wildly without considering the consequences. His words cannot be taken as certain. Only we must decide whether Zijuan’s request is to be granted, so that she may rise.” Lady Wang said, “It is no question of granting it or not. Once a person has made up her mind, there is no turning her from it. But then, what Baoyu said must be settled too.” At this, Zijuan kowtowed. Xichun also thanked Lady Wang. Zijuan then kowtowed to Baoyu and Baochai. Baoyu murmured, “Amitabha! How rare—how truly rare! Who would have thought that you would be the first to attain deliverance!” For all her self-command, Baochai could scarcely contain herself. Xiren alone, heedless even of Lady Wang’s presence, continued to weep bitterly. “I too wish to follow Fourth Miss into the religious life,” she said. Baoyu smiled. “Your intentions are good, but you are not destined to enjoy such serene blessings.” Xiren wept. “Then you mean I am destined to die!” Hearing this, Baoyu did feel grieved, but he could find no words. As it was already the fifth watch, Baoyu urged Lady Wang to retire, and Li Wan and the others dispersed. Caiping and the others attended Xichun for the time being and later were married off. Zijuan served her for the rest of her life, never wavering from her original resolve. But that belongs to the later story.

p.src: Meanwhile, Jia Zheng was escorting Grandmother Jia’s coffin southward. Troops and boats returning victorious from the campaign were passing through, crowding the waterways and preventing rapid progress, and the delay made him exceedingly anxious. Fortunately, he encountered some officials from the maritime frontier and learned that the Coastal Defense Commander had been summoned back to the capital by imperial command. Thinking that Tanchun would surely return home, he felt somewhat relieved. Yet he could not discover the date of their departure, and his impatience returned. Calculating that his travel funds would not suffice, he had no choice but to write to Lai Shangrong at his post, asking to borrow five hundred taels of silver and instructing a servant to bring the money to meet him along the route for necessary expenses. The messenger had been gone several days before Jia Zheng’s boat managed to travel a mere dozen or so li. When the servant returned and caught up with the boat, he presented Lai Shangrong’s written reply. In it Lai recounted all manner of hardships and enclosed fifty taels of silver. Jia Zheng read it angrily and ordered the servant to return the silver at once, sending the original letter back with word that Lai need trouble himself no further. The servant had no choice but to return to Lai Shangrong’s post.

p.src: When Lai Shangrong received the original letter and silver, he grew distressed, realizing that he had handled the matter inadequately. He added another hundred taels and begged the messenger to take it back and put in a good word for him. But the man refused to carry it back, dropped it there, and left. Uneasy at heart, Lai Shangrong immediately wrote home to explain matters to his father and ask him to find some way of obtaining leave and redeeming the family from servile status. The Lai family therefore asked Jia Qiang, Jia Yun, and others to plead with Lady Wang for the favor of releasing them. Jia Qiang knew perfectly well that it could not be done. After a day, he falsely reported that Lady Wang had refused. The Lai family applied for leave while also sending someone to Lai Shangrong’s post to tell him to plead illness and resign his office. Lady Wang knew nothing of any of this.

p.src: When Jia Yun heard Jia Qiang’s false report, he lost hope. Having also lost a considerable sum gambling outside over several days and having no means of repayment, he consulted Jia Huan. Jia Huan himself had not a penny. Although Concubine Zhao had amassed a small amount of savings, he had long since squandered it all; how could he help anyone else? Then he remembered how harshly Xifeng had treated him and conceived a plan to take advantage of Jia Lian’s absence by disposing of Qiaojie in revenge. Using this as bait for Jia Yun, he deliberately complained, “You are grown men, yet when there is money to be made you dare not undertake it, and instead come consulting someone penniless like me.” Jia Yun said, “Third Uncle, that is a strange thing to say. We may have played and made mischief together, but where was there ever any prospect of money?” Jia Huan said, “Did someone not say the other day that a prince from an outlying domain wanted to buy a concubine? Why do you not discuss with Uncle Wang the idea of giving Qiaojie to him?” Jia Yun replied, “Uncle, forgive me for saying something that may anger you, but if this foreign lord pays money to buy her, do you imagine he will still maintain relations with our family?” Jia Huan whispered something in Jia Yun’s ear. Though Jia Yun nodded, he regarded it merely as a child’s talk and paid it no serious attention. Just then Wang Ren came over and asked, “What are you two discussing? Are you keeping it from me?” Jia Yun whispered Jia Huan’s proposal into his ear. Wang Ren clapped his hands. “That is an excellent idea, and there is money in it too! I only fear that you lack the nerve. If you dare undertake it, I am her own maternal uncle and have the authority to decide. All that is needed is for Third Huan to mention it to the Elder Lady; I shall speak to Uncle Xing as well. When the ladies ask, you must all join together and say that it is a fine match.” Once Jia Huan and the others had settled their plan, Wang Ren went to seek Uncle Xing, while Jia Yun reported to Ladies Xing and Wang, embellishing the proposal until it sounded more splendid still.

p.src: What Lady Wang heard sounded plausible enough, but she still did not believe it. When Lady Xing heard that Uncle Xing knew about the matter, she was pleased and sent someone to fetch him for questioning. Uncle Xing had already heard Wang Ren's account and knew he could claim a share of the spoils, so he told Lady Xing, “As for this prince of a commandery, he is a man of the highest distinction. If we accept this marriage, although she may not become his principal wife, I guarantee that as soon as she enters his household, Brother-in-law will quickly regain his post and our family's influence here will revive.” Lady Xing had never possessed much judgment. Fooled into eagerness by her foolish brother's string of lies, she summoned Wang Ren, whose account made the prospect sound more splendid still. Lady Xing therefore sent someone out to catch up with Jia Yun and tell him. Wang Ren immediately found someone to carry the message to the residence of the tributary prince. Knowing nothing of the true circumstances, the tributary prince decided to send people to inspect the girl. Jia Yun also bribed the inspectors and explained, “This is being kept secret from the entire household; it is simply that the prince's household wishes to consider a match. Once the match is settled, her grandmother will approve it, and with her own maternal uncle acting as guarantor, there is nothing to fear.” The inspectors agreed. Jia Yun then sent word to Lady Xing and reported back to Lady Wang as well. Li Wan, Baochai, and the others, unaware of the true reason, assumed it was a good match and were all delighted.

p.src: Sure enough, several women arrived that day, all gorgeously made up and richly dressed. Lady Xing received them inside and exchanged some small talk with them. The visitors knew that she held an imperial title and did not dare treat her discourteously. Since nothing had yet been settled, Lady Xing had not explained matters to Qiaojie; she merely said that some relatives had come to visit and told the girl to meet them. Qiaojie was, after all, still a child and paid no attention to such matters, so she came over with her nurse. Ping'er, uneasy about it, followed them. Two of the women were dressed like palace attendants. On seeing Qiaojie, they looked her over from head to toe, then rose, took her by the hand, and examined her once more. After sitting only a little while, they left. Their scrutiny left Qiaojie blushing with embarrassment. Back in her room, she was puzzled; unable to recall any such relatives, she questioned Ping'er. Ping'er had recognized what sort of visitors they were and was almost certain that they had come to inspect Qiaojie for a marriage. “But Second Master Lian is away, and the senior lady is deciding matters. I still do not know which household they came from. If this were a proper match between equals, they should not have inspected her in this fashion. Judging by the manner of those women, they did not seem to belong to one of our dynasty's own princely houses, but rather to some outside domain. For now, there is no need to explain it to the young lady; let us first discover the truth.”

p.src: Ping'er quietly made a point of investigating. The maids and matrons had all served under Ping'er before, and when she questioned them, they told her every rumor they had heard from outside. Ping'er was so frightened that she did not know what to do. Without telling Qiaojie, she hurried to inform Li Wan and Baochai and begged them to tell Lady Wang. Realizing that the affair boded ill, Lady Wang went and spoke to Lady Xing about it. Unfortunately, Lady Xing believed her brother and Wang Ren. Suspecting instead that Lady Wang meant no good, she said, “My granddaughter is grown now, and since Lian is away, I still have the authority to decide this matter. Besides, it was investigated by her own granduncle and her own maternal uncle. Surely their information cannot be less reliable than anyone else's! In any case, I approve of the match. If anything should go wrong, neither Lian nor I will blame anyone else!”

p.src: Hearing this, Lady Wang was inwardly angry. She forced herself to exchange a few pleasantries, then left, related everything to Baochai, and wept. Baoyu consoled her: “Please do not distress yourself, Madam. As I see it, this affair will never come to pass. This too is a trial appointed by Qiaojie's fate. All you need do is leave it alone.” Lady Wang said, “Whenever you open your mouth, nonsense comes out. Once the agreement is made, they will come and take her away. If Ping'er is right, would your Second Cousin Lian not blame me? Even if she were not my own grandniece but merely a relative's child, I would still want her to make a good match. We arranged Miss Xing's marriage to your second elder brother-in-law. Are they not living together happily and harmoniously now? Miss Qin married into the Mei family, and I hear that she is very well provided for. As for Miss Shi, her marriage was her uncle's decision. At first all was well, but now her husband has died of consumption, and your Cousin Shi has resolved to remain a widow. Hers has become a hard life. If Qiaojie were mistakenly given to the wrong family, would that not show me to be heartless?” As they were speaking, Ping'er came to see Baochai and to learn what attitude Lady Xing had taken. Lady Wang repeated what Lady Xing had said. Ping'er stood stunned for a long while, then knelt and pleaded, “Qiaojie's whole future depends upon you, Madam. If you believe what those people say, not only will the young lady suffer all her life, but what shall we tell Second Master Lian when he returns?” Lady Wang said, “You are a sensible woman. Get up and listen to me. Qiaojie is, after all, the senior lady's granddaughter. If she insists on deciding the matter, how can I stop her?” Baoyu tried to reassure them: “It will do no harm. We need only understand the truth.” Ping'er feared that Baoyu, in one of his mad fits, might blurt the matter out. She said nothing further, took leave of Lady Wang, and went away.

She would not allow Baoyu or Baochai to come, saying that a little sleep would make her well. She remained deeply troubled herself, and when she heard that Aunt Li had arrived, she was in no state to receive her. p.src: Recently, our way has been crowded with victorious ships returning from the coastal frontier, so we have been unable to travel quickly. I hear that Sister Tan is coming to the capital with her father-in-law and husband; I wonder whether any word has arrived. I previously received a report from my nephew Lian and learned that the eldest master was unwell; I do not know whether any definite news has since arrived. Baoyu and Lan's examination date is drawing near; they must apply themselves earnestly and must not be idle. It will still be some days before the old lady's coffin reaches home. I am in good health, so there is no need to worry about me. Let Baoyu and the others be informed of these instructions. Written by my own hand, on the — day of the — month. Rong is to submit a separate report. After reading it, Lady Wang handed it back to Jia Lan and said, “Take it to show your second uncle, then give it to your mother.” As she was speaking, Li Wan and Aunt Li arrived. When they had exchanged greetings, Lady Wang invited them to sit. Aunt Li then related the Zhen family's proposal to marry Li Qi. They all discussed the matter for a while. Li Wan then asked Lady Wang, “Have you read the master's letter, madam?” “I have,” replied Lady Wang. Jia Lan took it over to show his mother. After reading it, Li Wan said, “Third Sister has been away for several years without coming back, but now she is returning to the capital. That must set your mind considerably at ease, madam.” Lady Wang said, “My heart was aching, but learning that Tan is coming back has made me feel a little better. I only wonder when she will arrive.” Aunt Li then asked whether Jia Zheng was well on his journey. Li Wan turned to Jia Lan and said, “You saw that, my boy? The examination is near, and your grandfather is worrying himself beyond measure about it. Hurry and take the letter to show your second uncle.” Aunt Li said, “Neither uncle nor nephew has ever attended the Imperial College, so how can they sit the examination?” Lady Wang replied, “When their grandfather set out to take up his post as Grain Intendant, he secured purchased studentships for both uncle and nephew.” Aunt Li nodded. Jia Lan came out with the letter in hand and went to look for Baoyu.

p.src: Meanwhile, after seeing Lady Wang off, Baoyu was savoring the essay “Autumn Floods.” Baochai came out from the inner room and, seeing him so absorbed that he had forgotten words themselves, went over to look. When she saw what he was reading, she felt deeply vexed. On reflection, she felt it could never end well if he persisted in treating such talk of renouncing the world and forsaking society as a serious concern. Judging from his present state that persuasion would be useless, she sat beside him in a daze. Seeing her like this, Baoyu asked, “What is troubling you now?” Baochai replied, “Since you and I are husband and wife, I regard you as the support on which my whole life depends; this has nothing to do with private sensual desire. Glory, rank, and riches are no more than fleeting clouds before one's eyes, but from ancient times the sages have placed the foundation of moral character above all else.” Before she had finished, Baoyu set the book aside and said with a faint smile, “You speak of the foundation of moral character and of the sages of old, but do you know that those sages said, ‘Do not lose the heart of a newborn child’? What virtue does a newborn child possess? It is merely without knowledge, understanding, greed, or inhibition. From birth we have already sunk into greed, anger, delusion, and attachment, as though into mire; how can we escape such a net of worldly dust? Only now do I understand the four words, ‘meetings and partings in this floating life.’ The ancients spoke them, yet they never awakened a single person. If we must discuss the foundation of moral character, who has ever attained the state of primal beginning?” Baochai replied, “Since you speak of the ‘heart of a newborn child,’ the sages of old understood loyalty and filial devotion to constitute that heart. They did not mean fleeing the world, forsaking society, and severing every bond. Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius kept the salvation of the people and the betterment of the world constantly in their hearts. The so-called heart of a newborn child amounts simply to the two words ‘unable to bear suffering.’ But by what you have just said, you can bear to abandon the bonds of kinship. How can that possibly be right?” Baoyu nodded and said with a smile, “Yao and Shun did not coerce Chao Fu and Xu You; King Wu and the Duke of Zhou did not coerce Bo Yi and Shu Qi.” Before he could finish, Baochai interrupted, “That argument is even more mistaken. If everyone in antiquity had been a Chao Fu, Xu You, Bo Yi, or Shu Qi, why do people today revere Yao, Shun, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius as sages? Besides, it is still more absurd for you to compare yourself to Bo Yi and Shu Qi. They lived in the troubled last days of the Shang dynasty and faced many impossible circumstances; only for that reason did they find a pretext to withdraw. We live in an age of enlightened rule; our family has received the nation's favor for generations, and our forefathers enjoyed robes of brocade and food of jade. Moreover, ever since your birth, the departed old lady and the master and mistress have cherished you like a precious jewel. Think over what you have just said and decide for yourself whether it is right or wrong.” Baoyu made no reply, but merely tilted his head back and smiled. Baochai continued to urge him, “Since reason has failed you and you have nothing more to say, I advise you to settle your mind from now on and apply yourself properly to your studies.

p.src: If only you can win a place in the examination, even if you stop there afterward, you will not have failed the grace of the sovereign or the virtue of your ancestors.” Baoyu nodded, sighed, and said, “Winning a place is really no difficult matter. But your words, ‘stop there afterward, and you will not have failed the grace of the sovereign or the virtue of your ancestors,’ do not stray from the essential point.” Before Baochai could reply, Xiren came over and said, “We do not understand the sages and worthies of old whom Second Mistress was just discussing. I only think of how all of us have followed Second Master since childhood, laboring and fretting, and taking no end of care to please you. It was our duty, to be sure, but Second Master ought to show us some consideration too. And Second Mistress has fulfilled so many filial duties toward the master and mistress on your behalf. Even if you attach no importance to the bond between husband and wife, you must not disappoint people's devotion so utterly. As for all that talk of immortals, it is even more obviously false. p.src: Xiren was about to say more when footsteps sounded outside, and someone asked through the window, “Is Second Uncle in the room?” Baoyu recognized Jia Lan’s voice. Rising, he said with a smile, “Come in.” Baochai also rose. Jia Lan entered beaming, paid his respects to Baoyu and Baochai, and asked after Xiren—who returned the courtesy—before presenting the letter to Baoyu. Baoyu took it and read it, then said, “Your Third Aunt is coming back.” Jia Lan said, “Since Grandfather has written so, she must indeed be coming back.” Baoyu nodded without speaking and fell into silent thought. Jia Lan then asked, “Uncle, did you see what Grandfather wrote at the end, telling us to apply ourselves to our studies? I fear you haven’t written any essays at all lately, Uncle?” Baoyu laughed. “I too must write a few pieces to get my hand in, so that I can go and swindle myself an official degree.” Jia Lan said, “If that is your intention, Uncle, set a few topics and let me write along with you. Then I too may scrape through the examination instead of handing in a blank paper and being laughed at. And they would not laugh at me alone—they would laugh at you too.” “You would hardly come to that,” said Baoyu. As they spoke, Baochai told Jia Lan to sit down. Baoyu remained in his former seat, while Jia Lan sat sideways beside him. They discussed composition for a while, and before long both faces shone with delight. Seeing uncle and nephew enjoying their discussion so much, Baochai withdrew once more into the inner room. Reflecting carefully on Baoyu’s present behavior, she thought that perhaps he had finally come to his senses; yet in their earlier conversation he had agreed only to the four words “stop from this point onward,” and she could not tell what he had meant by that. Baochai remained uncertain, but Xiren alone was overjoyed to see how readily he discussed essays and how pleased he became at the mention of sitting the examination. She thought, “Amitabha! After all our efforts, we have finally talked him round—as laboriously as expounding the Four Books!” While Baoyu and Jia Lan continued discussing composition, Ying’er brought in tea, and Jia Lan rose to receive it. They talked a while longer about the rules of the examination and about inviting Zhen Baoyu to join them, to which Baoyu also seemed quite willing to agree. Presently Jia Lan went home, leaving the letter with Baoyu.

p.src: Still holding the letter, Baoyu went inside smiling and handed it to Sheyue to put away. Then he came back out, put aside his copy of the Zhuangzi, and summoned Sheyue, Qiuwen, Ying’er, and the others to move several works of which he had always been especially fond—including the Cantong Qi, the Yuanming Bao, and the Wudeng Huiyuan—and set them all to one side. Baochai found this behavior most extraordinary. Wishing to test him, she asked with a smile, “It is proper enough not to read them, but why must you move them away?” Baoyu replied, “Only now have I come to understand. These books amount to nothing. I mean to burn them all in a single fire; only then will things be clean.” Hearing this, Baochai was more delighted than ever. But then she heard Baoyu softly chant, “In the scriptures’ words there is no Buddha-nature; beyond the alchemical art there lies an elixir of immortality.” Baochai did not hear him clearly; she caught only the phrases “no Buddha-nature” and “an elixir of immortality.” Doubt arose in her mind once more, and she resolved to watch what he would do. Baoyu ordered Sheyue, Qiuwen, and the others to prepare a quiet room and gather there all the collections of classical sayings, celebrated model essays, court compositions, and similar works. Then he truly settled down in silence and applied himself to study. Only then did Baochai set her mind at ease.

p.src: For Xiren, what she now heard and saw was altogether unprecedented. Smiling, she whispered to Baochai, “Your Ladyship truly explains things with perfect clarity. By pursuing that single line of argument, you have made Second Master understand at last. It is only a pity this has come a little late, with the examination already so near.” Baochai nodded and smiled. “Success and rank are ordained by fate; whether he passes or fails does not really depend on how early or late he begins his efforts. I ask only that from now on he devote himself wholeheartedly to the proper path and never again become entangled with those former demons and delusions.” At this point, seeing that no one else was in the room, she lowered her voice and continued, “It is certainly very good that he has repented and come back to his senses. There is only one concern: I fear he may relapse into his old failing and begin associating with the girls again. That would be no good either.” “Your Ladyship is right,” said Xiren. Only after Second Master put his faith in that monk did he grow distant from these girls. Now that he no longer believes the monk, I truly fear he may relapse into his old failing. As I see it, Your Ladyship and I are people Second Master has never paid much attention to in that way, and Zijuan has gone. That leaves only the four of them. Of those, Wu’er is rather bewitching. I hear her mother has petitioned First Mistress and Your Ladyship to let her leave and marry into another family. But for these next few days, she is still here after all. There is nothing especially wrong with Sheyue or Qiuwen, but in those earlier years both did engage in some playful improprieties with Second Master. When all is considered, Ying’er alone is someone Second Master has never paid much attention to, and besides, she is steady and sensible. I think it would be enough to have Ying’er lead the little maids in serving him tea and water. I do not know what Your Ladyship thinks.” Baochai said, “Those are precisely my own concerns. Your suggestion will do very well.” From then on, Ying’er was assigned to attend him together with the little maids.

I think it would be enough to have Ying’er lead the little maids in serving him tea and water. I do not know what Your Ladyship thinks.”
Baochai said, “Those are precisely my own concerns. Your suggestion will do very well.”
From then on, Ying’er was assigned to attend him together with the little maids.
